create.title: Endpoint-complete full-character block-energy and one-sided UNBAL reduction
create.statement_tex: For the literal Round-124 zero-extended dual rows put B_(p,n)=sum_(0<=a<H)b_(p,n+a), E_eq=C_H sum_(p,n)|B_(p,n)|^2, and E_chi=C_H sum_n|sum_(p>0 odd)chi_4(p)B_(p,n)|^2. Exact Fejer expansion gives E_eq=D_0+S_eq^(nonzero), E_chi=D_0+S_eq^(nonzero)+S_neq, hence S_off=E_chi-D_0 and S_neq=E_chi-E_eq. Since E_chi,D_0>=0 and D_0<<X^(1/2), S_off>=-D_0 and the absolute square-target estimate for S_off is equivalent to the single upper bound E_chi<<_epsilon X^(1/2+epsilon). Combining with Round 124 gives V_(M,H)=E_chi-Q_safe+O(1), so any fixed-power physical violation is positive and is exactly an excess of E_chi modulo proved packages. This is a sign localization and target-equivalent reduction, not the missing upper estimate.
create.next_action: The exact parked flat-smooth survivor is E_chi. Reopen only for a genuinely joint actual-character upper bound before any sectorwise norm, or for an endpoint-complete stronger inverse theorem.

create.title: Dual-sector coefficient obstruction, curvature ledger, and half-alias repair
create.statement_tex: For the same rows, the complete fixed-mode energy satisfies E_eq<<_epsilon X^epsilon min(X/D,D^2/L)=X^(1/2+epsilon)min(H,Q), where H=ceil(X^(1/2)/D), Q=D^2/(Lsqrt X), and both H,Q tend to infinity. Thus the reciprocal Q deficit is operative only for Q<=H; the uniform elementary loss is min(H,Q). Two identical long smooth rows in opposite chi_4 classes give exact coefficient controls with |S_eq^(nonzero)|,|S_neq|>>H D_0 but S_off=-D_0, so predetermined coefficient-blind sector bounds are fixed-power stronger than the target. On strict interiors the k-B-process has coefficient -2i/p, returned profile W(Xd/(DM))q_L((X/M)p), and Q dual labels, while a second B-process self-returns. Odd-p coherence requires E_d^*=M(d'-d)-2Add' and phase factor (-1)^A, not the incomplete 4a lattice. At fixed (n,d,d') the p-window has length O(1/H), and summing n first leaves an unresolved moving floor overlap. Hence cellwise Cauchy, a separate positive-row norm, re-Poissonization, and the proposed exact/far/near second-stage split do not prove the target. The stationary statements are principal-interior diagnostics, not a complete hard-block transform or a signed lower bound.
create.next_action: Freeze separate-sector positivity, cellwise norms, a universal Q-only ledger, the 4a alias lattice, and another one-variable B-process. Reopen only inside a complete actual-character inequality for E_chi.

reject.reason: The exact identities S_eq^(nonzero)=E_eq-D_0 and S_neq=E_chi-E_eq show that the entire positive fixed-mode energy can cancel between the sectors.
Positivity proves only S_off>=-D_0. It gives no upper bound for the full-character energy E_chi.
Two opposite-character identical smooth rows make both separate sectors of size at least H D_0 while their sum is -D_0.
When Q>H, the original H-term triangle is smaller than the reciprocal Q ledger. The best elementary loss is min(H,Q).
If K/D<1, the derivative crosses Q>H dual labels across only H primal spacings; the labels are not independent nonempty lattice cells.
Odd-p sums are coherent modulo one-half integers. The 4a lattice retains only even A and misses exact odd half-integer aliases.
The literal simultaneous saddle selectors leave a p-window of length D^2H/X asymptotic to 1/H, not L.
After summing n first, the exact p-dependent overlap has moving floor and hard-face jumps; no target-safe aggregate error ledger is proved.
Hard block faces, endpoint saddles, Fresnel transitions, inactive modes, support entries and exits, and aggregate errors are not included.
On strict interiors the second reciprocal B-process restores the original phase, coefficient, profile, and selector.
The complete bound is X^(1/2+epsilon)min(H,Q), and both H and Q tend to infinity; moreover E_eq is stronger than the target E_chi.
The required positive upper bound for E_chi is unproved, and every nonflat, hard, sharp, clipped, starred, arithmetic, and transition owner remains separate.
